newsitem.title: FINLAND: Softer forestries drag Helsinki from early peaks.
newsitem.headline: Softer forestries drag Helsinki from early peaks.

text.p: Shares were dragged by a correction in forestries on Monday and trade was modest as investors took a wait-and-see attitude as the corporate reporting season ended, brokers said.

The HEX general index ended 0.37 percent lower at 2,978.19 points after an early attempt in early trade to test the 3,000 mark failed after it hit a new 2,997.68 record. The correction was sparked by the weaker dollar.
The derivatives and portfolio benchmark FOX index closed down 0.68 percent at 1,045.69 points.
"There's been a bit of a hangover effect. We went up very fast on Friday," one broker said.

Forestry major UPM-Kymmene fell over four percent to end at 116.00 markka, down 5.50, and Enso -- the last blue-chip to report 1996 results -- fell 0.20 markka to 45.30 though its report and comments were largely in-line.

Telecoms group Nokia was active with interest on both sides but the share inched 0.50 markka lower to close at 318.50. The CeBIT technology and telecoms fair in Hanover maintained interest in telecoms, brokers said.

Among financials, Finland's largest banking group Merita rose 0.10 to 19.00 in healthy dealings, but insurer Pohjola fell 3.50 markka to 144.50 after reports the financial regulator would probe its information about plans to absorb mutual Suomi.
Confectionery and packaging group Huhtamaki which is expected to be acquisitive rose 9.00 markka to 246.00 in lively trade, and even its less liquid K share was active.
